description: Held out. A CV summary and two project entries for a named role, chosen from five candidate projects, from the candidate's rambling notes. The output should follow the CV sample: a summary of at most three sentences in the candidate's voice, two entries chosen for relevance with an action and a result each, no irrelevant projects, no claim of the standard the candidate has not worked with.
prompt: Write the CV summary and the two best project entries for the Tolliver clinical documentation writer role, from lucia-projects.md. Format like cv-sample.md. Save it to out/cv-snippets.md.

files.lucia-projects.md:
lucia-projects.md -- all the stuff I did that might count. Applying: Clinical Documentation Writer, Tolliver Medical Devices (infusion pumps).

A. Infusion pump quick guides, Ward Group 4 (2022–23). Old guide = 14 pages, nobody read it, agency nurses kept asking. I rewrote as 2-page laminated, with photos of the real pump screens. Agency nurse onboarding on the pump went from 3 h to 1.5 h (asked the ward educator, Rosalind, she timed 10 inductions before/after). Used on 6 wards. I did the writing + layout; nursing educators reviewed.
B. Pump alarm label test (2023). I ran a small usability test of the alarm-symbol stickers with 12 nurses (think-aloud, 25 min each). 3 labels confused people (the 'occlusion' one worst: 7 of 12 misread). Changed 3 labels, retest with 6 nurses: 0 misreads. Reported to the hospital's medical-devices committee.
C. Christmas rota spreadsheet for the ward (2021). 60 staff, swaps. Everyone loved it. Not relevant?
D. 6-week agile project course (2024, evening). Certificate.
E. Translated 8 patient leaflets to Portuguese (2023), volunteer.
Background: RN 9 yrs (adult ICU 2016-2025, ICU = intensive care). Now on secondment 80% in the education team. No IEC 62366 (usability standard) experience; no regulated-document system (e.g. Veeva) experience; I know the pump's workflows from the bedside.
Role ad wants: write instructions for use (IFU), run usability tests with clinicians, work with engineers. Desirable: IEC 62366, document control.
Output: 1 summary (3 sentences max) and the TWO best entries. Format like cv-sample.md. Don't pad.
files.cv-sample.md:
**Summary**
Software tester with six years in banking apps, now moving into accessibility work. I write test plans that engineers read to the end, and I have trained 20 colleagues to check screens with a screen reader.

**Accessibility audit of the mobile app, Hartwell Bank (2023)**
- Found that the balance screen could not be read aloud, and wrote the three-line fix that the developers adopted.
- Re-tested the 14 most-used screens afterwards; all 14 now pass.

**Screen-reader training, Hartwell Bank (2022–23)**
- Ran six one-hour sessions for 20 testers, using a short checklist I wrote.
- Eleven of them now apply it to their own releases without being asked.

checks.note: the usability test entry is chosen

checks.pattern: (?i)(?:\b3 hours?|three hours?|\b3 h\b)[^.\n]{0,40}(?:1\.5|90 min|an hour and a half)

controls.name: good
controls.output:
**Summary**
Intensive care nurse of nine years, now on secondment in my hospital's education team, writing the guides that ward nurses use. I know the infusion pump from the bedside and have tested its labels with the nurses who use them. I have not worked with IEC 62366 or a regulated document system.

**Infusion pump quick guides, Ward Group 4 (2022–23)**
- Rewrote a 14-page guide nobody read as a two-page laminated card with photos of the real pump screens.
- Agency nurse onboarding on the pump fell from 3 hours to 1.5 hours, timed over 10 inductions; the card is used on 6 wards.

**Pump alarm label test (2023)**
- Ran think-aloud usability tests of the alarm stickers with 12 nurses; 7 of 12 misread the occlusion label.
- Changed three labels; no nurse in the retest of 6 misread them. Reported to the hospital's medical-devices committee.
controls.reply: Saved the summary and two entries to out/cv-snippets.md. I left out the rota spreadsheet, the agile course and the leaflet translations as less relevant. Your notes say you have no IEC 62366 or document-system experience, so the summary says so.
